claims.text: The as-built Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an FCC microstructure.
The starting-state alloy has a homogeneous elemental distribution.
The starting-state alloy has minimal oxide presence.
Under high-temperature oxidizing conditions, oxygen preferentially diffuses along grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary oxygen transport oxidizes Cr, Al, and Ti.
Oxidation causes localized depletion of Cr, Al, and Ti at grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary oxidation forms continuous or semi-continuous brittle oxide networks.
Brittle grain-boundary oxide networks reduce intergranular cohesion.
Reduced intergranular cohesion facilitates catastrophic crack propagation under thermal or mechanical stress.
Samples exposed to high oxygen partial pressure will show more grain-boundary oxidation and Cr, Al, and Ti depletion than the starting-state baseline.
High-oxygen exposure will lead to embrittlement and catastrophic failure under thermal cycling or mechanical loading.
A 90% Ar/10% H2 reducing atmosphere suppresses oxidation relative to oxidizing atmospheres.
Suppressing oxidation prevents brittle oxide-network formation and preserves grain-boundary cohesion.
Samples exposed to reducing gas will retain better mechanical integrity than samples exposed to high oxygen partial pressure.
Oxidation, rather than phase transformation, is the predominant cause of the proposed degradation.
A critical oxygen partial-pressure threshold exists above which grain-boundary oxidation triggers catastrophic failure.
The proposed degradation pathway applies over 900–1100°C and exposure durations of 24–72 hours.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism state that control experiments will confirm or ensure that non-oxidative mechanisms do not drive failure, whereas the uncertainty field acknowledges that other contributing mechanisms may not be completely excluded.
